今天的主题：科技、屏幕时间和孩子成长。这组词对 G 类特别实用：写作 Task 2 常考「孩子该不该限制使用手机」「科技对教育利大于弊吗」；口语 Part 1 的 Mobile Phones、Internet，Part 3 的 children and technology 都能直接用；G 类阅读里的家长须知、学校通知也常出现 device、access、guideline 这类词。

例句

  • Many parents want to restrict their children's access to social media.（很多家长想限制孩子使用社交媒体。）
  • Spending excessive time on a device can lead to a sedentary lifestyle.（在设备上花过多时间会导致久坐的生活方式。）
  • Some apps are designed to be addictive, so children find it hard to concentrate.（有些应用被设计得让人上瘾，所以孩子很难集中注意力。）
  • Used in a moderate way, technology can enable children to learn faster.（适度使用的话，科技能让孩子学得更快。）
  • The government has issued new guidelines as a practical measure to protect young users.（政府发布了新的指导方针，作为保护未成年用户的实际措施。）

过关标准：遮住中文看英文，能说出 22 个以上的意思，再挑 5 个自己造句（试试用 restrict、excessive、moderate 写一句你对孩子用手机的看法，Task 2 和口语 Part 3 都能直接用）。

BBC 6 Minute English：Limiting screen time for children（限制孩子的屏幕时间）。这集讲很多家长担心孩子花太多时间在手机平板上，澳大利亚已经禁止 16 岁以下用社交媒体。剑桥大学研究员说重点不是让孩子远离科技，而是用得有目的；临床心理学家建议做一些小改变，比如把设备挪到孩子看不见的地方。这集句子短、语速不快，又和你要去的澳大利亚有关，很适合精听。音频和原文都已经放在页面里，不用打开 BBC 网站。

  1. 先把上面的听前生词过一遍，听不太懂可以先读懂原文再听。
  2. 第一遍不看文字，只听大意，回答开头的问题：根据英国媒体监管机构的数据，三到四岁的孩子里有多少拥有智能手机？a) one in twenty b) one in ten c) one in five。顺便听出：去年年底哪个国家禁止 16 岁以下使用社交媒体？贝基建议家长把设备放到哪里？
  3. 第二遍点开下面的原文精听，听不出的地方暂停、倒回去并标出来。Dr Emily Goodacre 和 Dr Becky Kennedy 两段是真实录音，语速稍快，多听几遍，尤其是 Emily 讲 intentional 和 the bar needs to be higher 那段。
  4. 第三遍挑 Becky 那段（"You can even say to a kid, you know why I moved it?..."）跟读，模仿语调和连读。
  5. 记住 6 个表达：intentional（有目的的，刻意的）、the bar needs to be higher（标准需要提高）、enable（使能够，促成）、eager（渴望的）、shift（小变化，转变）、set someone up for something（让某人为某事做好准备）。
点开看原文（难词带中文，点虚线词显示）
💡 点击或悬停虚线词看中文；点击说话人名字可单独切换该段翻译

Neil：Hello, this is 6 Minute English from BBC Learning English. I'm Neil.

Neil：大家好，这里是 BBC 学习英语的《六分钟英语》。我是尼尔。

Becca：And I'm Becca. Neil, I've noticed that you're pretty good at not checking your phone at work. How much time do you spend on your phone outside of work?

Becca：我是贝卡。尼尔，我发现你上班时挺能忍住不看手机的。那下班以后你花多少时间在手机上？

Neil：Yes, I probably was. You know, Becca, I spend far too much实在太多 time looking at my phone, and I really don't like it. How about you?

Neil：嗯，可能吧。你知道吗，贝卡，我花在看手机上的时间实在太多了，我自己也很不喜欢这样。你呢？

Becca：I don't think you're alone不止你一个人这样. I also spend way too much太多了（口语） time looking at my phone.

Becca：我觉得不止你一个人这样。我也花了太多时间看手机。

Neil：Well, Becca, we are both adults, but today we're talking about screen time屏幕时间（用电子设备的时间） and children's screen time屏幕时间（用电子设备的时间）. Screen time屏幕时间（用电子设备的时间） – that's how much time you spend using devices设备 like smartphones, tablets平板电脑 and laptops笔记本电脑.

Neil：嗯，贝卡，我们俩都是成年人，但今天我们要聊的是屏幕时间，而且是孩子的屏幕时间。屏幕时间，就是你使用智能手机、平板和笔记本电脑这些设备的时长。

Becca：Yes, and it's a particular worry of many parents that their children spend too much time on these devices设备. At the end of last year, Australia banned access to social media apps社交媒体应用 for under 16s16 岁以下的人, and countries like the UK are considering similar measures类似的措施.

Becca：对，很多家长特别担心孩子在这些设备上花太多时间。去年年底，澳大利亚禁止 16 岁以下的人使用社交媒体应用，英国等国家也在考虑类似的措施。

Neil：So, why is this? In this episode, we'll hear from a clinical临床的 psychologist心理学家 and research associate研究员 at the University of Cambridge talking about screen time屏幕时间（用电子设备的时间） and children. As usual, we'll be learning some useful new words and phrases. And remember, you'll find all this episode's vocabulary, along with a transcript, on our website, bbclearningenglish.com.

Neil：那这是为什么呢？这一集我们会听一位临床心理学家和一位剑桥大学的研究员谈屏幕时间和孩子。和往常一样，我们会学一些有用的新词和短语。别忘了，本集所有词汇和文字稿都可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到。

Becca：But first Neil, I have a question for you. According to the UK media regulator媒体监管机构, how many children aged three to four have a smartphone? Is it:
a) one in twenty
b) one in ten, or
c) one in five?

Becca：不过尼尔，先问你一个问题。根据英国媒体监管机构的数据，三到四岁的孩子里有多少拥有智能手机？是 a) 二十分之一，b) 十分之一，还是 c) 五分之一？

Neil：Wow. Well, I'm going to guess 1 in 20, but I think it's probably more than that.

Neil：哇。嗯，我猜二十分之一，不过我觉得实际可能比这多。

Becca：Well, we'll find out弄清楚，得知 the answer later. Dr Emily Goodacre is a research associate研究员 at the University of Cambridge. Here, she tells Shiona McCallum, presenter主持人 of BBC World Service programme Tech Life, her thoughts on whether we should take away拿走 children's screen devices设备 completely.

Becca：好，答案稍后揭晓。埃米莉·古德克博士是剑桥大学的研究员。下面她对 BBC 世界服务节目《科技生活》的主持人希奥娜·麦卡勒姆谈了她的看法：我们是否应该把孩子的屏幕设备完全拿走。

Dr Emily Goodacre：Yeah, I think it's not as much as getting them away from technology but being intentional有目的的，刻意的 about how we use technology with children. For me, the bar absolutely needs to be higher标准绝对需要提高, and therefore I think about how to design products that think about childhood童年 first and really think about how children at different stages learn and develop and then see if there's a way that technology can enable使能够，促成 that.

Dr Emily Goodacre：嗯，我觉得重点不在于让孩子远离科技，而在于我们和孩子一起使用科技时要有明确的目的。对我来说，标准绝对需要提高，所以我会思考怎样设计产品，让产品首先考虑童年，真正考虑不同阶段的孩子是怎样学习和成长的，然后再看科技有没有办法促成这一点。

Neil：Emily highlights强调 how, rather than stopping children from using technology, parents need to be more intentional有目的的，刻意的 about how their children use it. An intention意图，打算 is a plan or reason to do something. So, to be intentional有目的的，刻意的 is to act with that plan or reason in mind心里带着这个计划或理由. It may make you act more carefully as a result.

Neil：埃米莉强调，与其阻止孩子使用科技，家长更需要对孩子怎么用科技有明确的目的。intention 是做某事的计划或理由。所以 intentional 就是心里带着这个计划或理由去做事。这样做的结果可能会让你行动更谨慎。

Becca：Emily also says the bar needs to be higher标准需要提高. The idiom习语 the bar is low标准很低 means that the standards, expectations期望, or requirements要求 are minimal极少的，最低的 and very easy to meet很容易达到. Therefore, she believes that the bar needs to be higher标准需要提高 – parents need to make their expectations期望 higher. They need to think or act more carefully when considering how much time children spend with technology. You might also hear people say set the bar higher把标准定高 or lower.

Becca：埃米莉还说标准需要提高。习语 the bar is low 意思是标准、期望或要求很低，很容易达到。所以她认为标准要提高，家长要提高期望。在考虑孩子花多少时间在科技产品上时，他们需要更认真地思考和行动。你也可能听到人们说 set the bar higher or lower（把标准定高或定低）。

Neil：Emily believes that being more intentional有目的的，刻意的 and setting the bar higher把标准定得更高 will enable使能够，促成 children to learn and develop alongside与……一起，在……旁边 technology. If you enable使能够，促成 something, you encourage somebody's ability to do something, or to make something possible.

Neil：埃米莉认为，更有目的性、把标准定得更高，能让孩子在使用科技的同时学习和成长。enable 某事，就是促进某人做某事的能力，或者让某事成为可能。

Becca：Now let's hear Dr Becky Kennedy, a clinical临床的 psychologist心理学家 and founder创始人 of an online parenting育儿 platform, talking about how parents feel about tech and children, for BBC World Service programme Tech Life:

Becca：现在我们来听贝基·肯尼迪博士的说法。她是一位临床心理学家，也是一个在线育儿平台的创始人。她在 BBC 世界服务节目《科技生活》里谈家长对科技和孩子的感受：

Dr Becky Kennedy：I find parents are very, very eager渴望的 to understand what's really happening around technology in kids and then have practical, realistic现实可行的 things they can do in their home to make little shifts小变化，转变 that feel better.

Dr Becky Kennedy：我发现家长非常非常渴望了解孩子和科技之间到底发生了什么，然后希望有一些实际、可行的办法，在家里做一些小小的改变，让大家感觉更好。

Neil：Becky has found that many parents are eager渴望的 to understand their children's use of technology. Eager渴望的 is an adjective that describes wanting to do or have something very much.

Neil：贝基发现很多家长渴望了解孩子使用科技的情况。eager 是形容词，表示非常想做某事或非常想得到某物。

Becca：Becky also talks about making little shifts小变化，转变. A shift小变化，转变 is a small change. It can be used as a verb or a noun. Becky shares an example of a shift小变化，转变 that can help parents reduce children's screen time屏幕时间（用电子设备的时间）, moving the device设备 somewhere it can't be seen:

Becca：贝基还谈到做一些小小的 shift（改变）。shift 就是小的变化，可以当动词也可以当名词。贝基举了一个能帮家长减少孩子屏幕时间的小改变的例子：把设备挪到看不见的地方。

Dr Becky Kennedy：You can even say to a kid, you know why I moved it? It's actually because it's a really hard thing for me to expect from you, to see a screen in a room and not want to use it. I wasn't setting you up for success给你创造成功的条件.

Dr Becky Kennedy：你甚至可以对孩子说：你知道我为什么把它挪走吗？其实是因为，让你看到房间里有块屏幕却不想去用，这对你要求太高了。我之前没有给你创造成功的条件。

Neil：Becky explains how it's difficult for children to be expected to reduce their screen time屏幕时间（用电子设备的时间） if they can see their device设备. Having the device设备 in view在视线内 doesn't set them up for success给他们创造成功的条件. If you set someone up for something让某人为某事做好准备, you prepare them for it.

Neil：贝基解释说，如果孩子能看到自己的设备，却要求他们减少屏幕时间，这很难做到。设备就在眼前，并没有给他们创造成功的条件。set someone up for something 就是让某人为某事做好准备。

Becca：Yes. For example, earlier, I set Neil up for a shock when I asked him a question about screen time屏幕时间（用电子设备的时间）. Neil, I asked you, according to the UK media regulator媒体监管机构, how many children aged three to four have a smartphone.

Becca：对。比如刚才我问尼尔屏幕时间的问题，就给他准备了一个惊吓。尼尔，我问你：根据英国媒体监管机构的数据，三到四岁的孩子里有多少拥有智能手机。

Neil：And I said 1 in 20.

Neil：我说的是二十分之一。

Becca：Well, it is in fact c) 1 in 5.

Becca：其实答案是 c，五分之一。

Neil：Wow. I thought it might be more than I said. Now, let's recap回顾 the vocabulary we've learned, starting with intentional有目的的，刻意的. It's an adjective that describes acting with a plan or reason in mind.

Neil：哇。我就觉得可能比我说的多。现在我们来复习一下学过的词汇，先从 intentional 开始。这是形容词，表示带着计划或理由去做事，有目的的。

Becca：We had the expression the bar needs to be higher标准需要提高. To set the bar higher把标准定高 is to make your expectations期望 higher.

Becca：我们学了 the bar needs to be higher（标准需要提高）。set the bar higher 就是提高你的期望。

Neil：We also had enable使能够，促成. This is to encourage someone's ability to do something, or to make something possible.

Neil：我们还学了 enable，意思是促进某人做某事的能力，或者让某事成为可能。

Becca：To be eager渴望的 is to want to do or have something very much.

Becca：eager 就是非常想做某事或非常想得到某物。

Neil：A shift小变化，转变 is a small change. You can also use it as a verb to mean changing something slightly稍微.

Neil：shift 是小的变化。也可以当动词，意思是稍微改变某事。

Becca：And if you set someone up for something让某人为某事做好准备, you prepare them for it. Once again, our six minutes are up. If you enjoyed this episode, you'll find a quiz and worksheet练习题 to practise the vocabulary we've learnt on our website, bbclearningenglish.com. See you again soon. But for now, it's goodbye.

Becca：如果你 set someone up for something，就是让某人为某事做好准备。好了，六分钟又到了。如果你喜欢这一集，可以在我们的网站 bbclearningenglish.com 上找到测验和练习题，练习今天学的词汇。下次再见，现在先说再见。

Neil：Goodbye!

Neil：再见！

过关标准：不看原文能用中文说出这集讲了什么（家长担心什么、澳大利亚的做法、两位专家各自的建议），6 个表达都知道意思，Becky 那段能流利读下来。

小练习

  1. She was very ______ to start her new job.（渴望的）
  2. We need to be more ______ about how we spend our free time.（有目的的）
  3. The new app will ______ students to study anywhere.（使能够）
  4. A small ______ in your daily routine can make a big difference.（小变化）
  5. Good teachers set their students up ______ success.（介词）
  6. Customers expect more now, so the bar needs to be ______.（更高）
点开看答案

开头那题选 c，one in five，五分之一。尼尔猜的是二十分之一，猜少了。禁止 16 岁以下使用社交媒体的是澳大利亚；贝基建议把设备挪到孩子看不见的地方。填空：1. eager 2. intentional 3. enable 4. shift 5. for 6. higher

今天的小思考（为口语 Part 3 和大作文做准备）：Should the government ban social media for children under 16, like Australia? 用英语说两三句：I think it's a good idea because ... / Some people argue that ..., but I believe parents should ...。也可以想想：你小时候用手机多吗？你会怎样管自己孩子的屏幕时间？
